newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds set for rally, but cautious.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds set for rally, but cautious.

text.p: September T-bond futures should benefit from weakening European bond markets, but heavy overhead supply means gains could be limited, analysts said on Monday.
Although technically possible, a rally above the May congestion area to the 109-12 peak was unlikely before Friday's payrolls data which should signal interest rate moves in July.
"Generally the chart is pretty constructive," said Bill Westgate, vice president at HSBC Securities in London.
But he saw resistance immediately at the current 109-24. If that broke, the next barrier was the 110-00, 110-04 area, and the top of a seven month down trend channel coming at 110-09.
"I think we'll hold off before we get to Friday. There is pressure towards the up end of the range. I don't think we'll see a break before we see what happens to non-farm payrolls," Westgate said.
But overall, the negative sentiment about European debt markets should boost the U.S., he said.
"No matter what your political persuasion or your economic understanding of the whole EMU is, nobody can deny the fact that...(Europe) is a real environment of uncertainty."
He put the upside target at the February high of 113-09.
By 1025 GMT, September T-bonds were up 4/32 at 109-24.
Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) said Friday's surge to a peak of 109-26 had briefly topped the 73.6 percent retracement of the whole rally from 107-02 to 110-09, at 109-25.
"The large rally highlights our long held concern that, based on Elliott Wave counts, futures could punch out new highs before the bear market resumes," DMG said in a research note.
Given that a 50 percent retracement was attained on the way down to 108-05 on May 27, a move to 110-26 could be projected.
But futures should top toward the middle or end of this week after challenging 110-09, DMG said. They should then head down.
By 1035, the September Eurodollar was up 0.010 at 94.015.
